proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(S\in\mathcal P_k\), a selected table \(y\) compatible with \(\mathcal M_N\), and an array \(Y\in\mathcal M_N\) that generates \(y\).  Let \(\mu\) be its cell-mean surface.  For a nonneutral action and a matching anchor \(c\in T_{xa}(S)\), monotonicity and the Lipschitz inequality in \(\mathrm{def{:}response\text{-}class}\) imply
\[
\mu_{xa}(t)
\geq y_{cx}-\Gamma(m_c-t)_+,
\qquad
\mu_{xa}(t)
\leq y_{cx}+\Gamma(t-m_c)_+.
\tag{1}
\]
Indeed, if \(m_c\geq t\), the first inequality is the Lipschitz bound and the second follows from monotonicity; if \(m_c\leq t\), the roles reverse.  For the neutral action, invariance gives \(\mu_{x a_0}(t)=y_{cx}\) at every matching anchor.  Combining (1) with \(0\leq\mu_{xa}(t)\leq1\), and then taking the maximum of the lower bounds and the minimum of the upper bounds in \(\mathrm{def{:}envelopes}\), gives
\[
\ell_{xa}(t;y)\leq\mu_{xa}(t)\leq u_{xa}(t;y).
\tag{2}
\]
The weights satisfy \(q_x=N_x/N>0\).  Multiplying (2) at \(a=\pi(x)\), \(t=m_\pi\) by \(q_x\), summing over the finite set \(\mathcal X\), and using the definitions of \(L_S\), \(U_S\), and \(V_\mu\), yields
\[
L_S(\pi;y)
\leq V_\mu(\pi)
\leq U_S(\pi;y).
\tag{3}
\]

Define two complete surfaces simultaneously for every cell and action by
\[
\mu^-_{xa}(t)=\ell_{xa}(t;y),
\qquad
\mu^+_{xa}(t)=u_{xa}(t;y).
\tag{4}
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}envelope\text{-}feasibility}\), the surfaces in (4) are bounded, monotone and \(\Gamma\)-Lipschitz for nonneutral actions, constant for the neutral action, ordered, and equal to every selected anchor.  Homogenize them within cells:
\[
Y_i^-(a,t)=\mu^-_{x_i a}(t),
\qquad
Y_i^+(a,t)=\mu^+_{x_i a}(t).
\tag{5}
\]
The properties just listed hold unit by unit in (5), so both arrays belong not only to \(\mathcal M_N\) but to the individual-level subclass \(\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO},\Gamma}\).  Since \(N_x>0\), averaging (5) within cell \(x\) recovers (4), and anchor agreement implies that both arrays generate the same table \(y\).  Therefore, for every \(\pi\in\mathcal F\),
\[
V_{\mu^-}(\pi)
=\sum_xq_x\ell_{x,\pi(x)}(m_\pi;y)
=L_S(\pi;y),
\qquad
V_{\mu^+}(\pi)
=U_S(\pi;y).
\tag{6}
\]
Thus the two arrays in (5) are common lower and upper schedules for the entire library.

For \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), set
\[
Y_i^\lambda(a,t)=(1-\lambda)Y_i^-(a,t)+\lambda Y_i^+(a,t).
\]
Convex combinations preserve the range \([0,1]\), monotonicity, the \(\Gamma\)-Lipschitz inequality, neutral invariance, and all anchor equalities.  Hence \(Y^\lambda\in\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO},\Gamma}\subseteq\mathcal M_N\), and linearity of cell averages and policy values gives
\[
V_{\mu^\lambda}(\pi)
=(1-\lambda)L_S(\pi;y)+\lambda U_S(\pi;y).
\tag{7}
\]
As \(\lambda\) ranges over \([0,1]\), (7) fills the whole interval in (3).  This proves the claimed identified set.  Moreover, the bridge lemma shows that the attainable induced mean surfaces under \(\mathcal M_N\) and \(\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO},\Gamma}\) coincide.  Hence the same exact interval and the same homogeneous common endpoint schedules hold when the identifying class is restricted to the source-faithful individual-level Lipschitz subclass.

Fix \(S\in\mathcal P_k\), a compatible table \(y\), a future policy \(\pi\), and a cell \(x\).  Put \(a=\pi(x)\) and \(t=m_\pi\).  If \(T_{xa}(S)=\varnothing\), boundedness of the envelopes gives
\[
u_{xa}(t;y)-\ell_{xa}(t;y)\leq1=r_{\pi x}(S).
\tag{1}
\]
If \(a=a_0\) and \(T_{x a_0}(S)\neq\varnothing\), neutral invariance and compatibility make all neutral anchors equal, so the two neutral envelopes agree and their gap is
\[
0=r_{\pi x}(S).
\tag{2}
\]
Now suppose \(a\neq a_0\) and take any \(c\in T_{xa}(S)\).  If \(m_c\leq t\), the envelope definitions imply
\[
\ell_{xa}(t;y)\geq y_{cx},
\qquad
u_{xa}(t;y)\leq y_{cx}+\Gamma(t-m_c),
\]
while if \(m_c\geq t\), they imply
\[
\ell_{xa}(t;y)\geq y_{cx}-\Gamma(m_c-t),
\qquad
u_{xa}(t;y)\leq y_{cx}.
\]
Together with the unit range of the envelopes, both cases give
\[
u_{xa}(t;y)-\ell_{xa}(t;y)
\leq\min\{1,\Gamma|t-m_c|\}.
\tag{3}
\]
Taking the minimum of (3) over matching anchors, and combining it with (1)--(2), yields
\[
u_{x,\pi(x)}(m_\pi;y)-\ell_{x,\pi(x)}(m_\pi;y)
\leq r_{\pi x}(S).
\tag{4}
\]
Since \(q_x>0\), summing (4), maximizing over the finite nonempty set \(\mathcal F\), and then taking the supremum over \(Y\in\mathcal M_N\) gives
\[
\overline W(S)\leq\max_{\pi\in\mathcal F}R_\pi(S).
\tag{5}
\]

For the reverse inequality, finiteness of \(\mathcal F\) supplies a maximizer \(\pi^\star\) of \(R_\pi(S)\).  For each \(x\), write
\[
a=\pi^\star(x),
\qquad t=m_{\pi^\star},
\qquad w=r_{\pi^\star x}(S).
\]
If \(a\neq a_0\) and there is no matching anchor, define \(g_x^-=0\) and \(g_x^+=1\).  If there is a matching anchor and \(w=0\), define both functions to be zero.  In the remaining case \(a\neq a_0\), there is a matching anchor and \(w>0\); then \(\Gamma>0\), and define
\[
g_x^-(s)=\min\{w,\max\{0,\Gamma(s-t)\}\},
\qquad
g_x^+(s)=\min\{w,\max\{0,\Gamma(s-t)+w\}\}.
\tag{6}
\]
Composition with clipping to \([0,w]\) preserves monotonicity and cannot increase a Lipschitz constant, so the functions in (6) are bounded, nondecreasing, and \(\Gamma\)-Lipschitz.  The definition of \(w\) implies
\[
\Gamma|m_c-t|\geq w
\quad\text{for every }c\in T_{xa}(S).
\tag{7}
\]
If \(m_c<t\), equations (6)--(7) give \(g_x^-(m_c)=g_x^+(m_c)=0\); if \(m_c>t\), they give \(g_x^-(m_c)=g_x^+(m_c)=w\).  Equality \(m_c=t\) would imply \(w=0\), excluded in this case.  Hence the two functions agree at all matching anchors and satisfy
\[
g_x^-(t)=0,
\qquad g_x^+(t)=w.
\tag{8}
\]
For \(a=a_0\), use identical zero constants if a matching anchor exists and the two constants zero and one if none exists.  These functions are invariant in score, agree at every selected neutral anchor, and differ at the target by \(w\).

For each cell, use this pair for the target action \(a=\pi^\star(x)\), and use the identical zero function for every other action.  Define homogeneous fixed arrays from these cell surfaces.  The construction is bounded, monotone, \(\Gamma\)-Lipschitz, and neutral-invariant unit by unit; hence both arrays lie in \(\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO},\Gamma}\subseteq\mathcal M_N\).  At every selected arm-cell pair they agree: matching target-action anchors agree by (7)--(8), and all other actions are zero in both arrays.  Denote their common selected table by \(y^\star\).  Their values at \(\pi^\star\) differ by
\[
V_{\mu^+}(\pi^\star)-V_{\mu^-}(\pi^\star)
=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}q_xr_{\pi^\star x}(S)
=R_{\pi^\star}(S).
\tag{9}
\]
The sharp-common-endpoints theorem applied to \(y^\star\) places both values in the same sharp interval, so that interval has width at least (9).  The upper bound (5) forces equality, proves that the supremum is attained, and gives
\[
\overline W(S)
=\max_{\pi\in\mathcal F}R_\pi(S)
=\max_{\pi\in\mathcal F}\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}q_x
\min\bigl(\{1\}\cup\{d_{\pi xc}:c\in S\}\bigr).
\tag{10}
\]
The bridge lemma shows that restricting the supremum in \(\overline W(S)\) to \(\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO},\Gamma}\) leaves it unchanged; independently, the attaining arrays just constructed already lie in that subclass.  Thus (10) is also the exact prospective-width identity over the individual-level Lipschitz refinement.

Every \(q_x=N_x/N\) is rational.  Every \(d_{\pi xc}\) is rational because \(m_c\), \(m_\pi\), and \(\Gamma\) are rational, and all minima, sums, and maxima in (10) range over finite sets.  Hence \(\overline W(S)\) is rational for every panel.  The family \(\mathcal P_k\) is finite and nonempty because it contains \(\varnothing\); therefore its minimum \(D^\star\) is rational and attained.

added_lemmas.statement:
The individual-level Lipschitz class satisfies
\[
\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO},\Gamma}\subseteq\mathcal M_N.
\]
Conversely, for every \(Y\in\mathcal M_N\) there is a homogeneous-within-cell array \(\widetilde Y\in\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO},\Gamma}\) whose induced cell-mean surface equals that of \(Y\) at every \((x,a,t)\).  Consequently the sets of induced cell-mean surfaces, selected mean tables, and policy values generated by \(\mathcal M_N\) and by \(\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO},\Gamma}\) coincide.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(Y\in\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO},\Gamma}\).  Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\), \(a\neq a_0\), and \(0\leq s\leq t\leq1\).  The individual monotonicity in \(\mathrm{def{:}chen\text{-}oberst\text{-}individual\text{-}class}\) and \(N_x>0\) give
\[
\mu_{xa}(t)-\mu_{xa}(s)
=\frac1{N_x}\sum_{i:x_i=x}\{Y_i(a,t)-Y_i(a,s)\}\geq0.
\]
The triangle inequality and the individual Lipschitz condition in \(\mathrm{def{:}chen\text{-}oberst\text{-}gamma\text{-}subclass}\) give
\[
|\mu_{xa}(t)-\mu_{xa}(s)|
\leq\frac1{N_x}\sum_{i:x_i=x}|Y_i(a,t)-Y_i(a,s)|
\leq\Gamma|t-s|.
\]
For the neutral action, individual invariance gives
\[
\mu_{x a_0}(t)-\mu_{x a_0}(s)
=\frac1{N_x}\sum_{i:x_i=x}\{Y_i(a_0,t)-Y_i(a_0,s)\}=0.
\]
Every mean lies in \([0,1]\) because it is an average of numbers in \([0,1]\).  These are exactly the membership conditions in \(\mathrm{def{:}response\text{-}class}\), proving the inclusion.

For the converse, let \(Y\in\mathcal M_N\), let \(\mu\) be its induced cell-mean surface, and define
\[
\widetilde Y_i(a,t)=\mu_{x_i a}(t)
\quad(i\in\mathcal I, a\in\mathcal A, t\in[0,1]).
\]
The range, monotonicity, Lipschitz, and neutral-invariance requirements for \(\widetilde Y\) follow componentwise from the membership of \(Y\) in \(\mathcal M_N\).  Hence \(\widetilde Y\in\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO},\Gamma}\).  Moreover, using the definition of \(N_x\) and its positivity,
\[
\frac1{N_x}\sum_{i:x_i=x}\widetilde Y_i(a,t)
=\frac1{N_x}\sum_{i:x_i=x}\mu_{xa}(t)
=\mu_{xa}(t).
\]
Thus homogenization preserves the entire cell-mean surface.  Selected mean tables and policy values are functions only of that surface by the definitions of \(y\) and \(V_\mu\), so their attainable sets coincide as claimed.
added_lemmas.justification: This bridge proves that the aggregate mean formulation and the source-faithful individual-level \(\Gamma\)-Lipschitz subclass generate exactly the same observable mean surfaces and causal policy values.
added_lemmas.gap: ChenOberst2025 uses unit-level performance monotonicity and neutral-action equality; the bridge records precisely how the present finite-population mean model relates to that class after adding individual-level Lipschitz smoothness.
added_lemmas.consumer: A reviewer can audit the class comparison without treating an aggregate restriction as if it were the published individual-level assumption.

added_lemmas.statement: Suppose \(\mathcal A\setminus\{a_0\}\neq\varnothing\) and some cell \(x_\star\) contains at least two units.  Then there is a bounded array in \(\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO}}\setminus\mathcal M_N\), and there is a bounded array in \(\mathcal M_N\setminus\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO}}\).  Thus, on such nondegenerate fixed populations, the unrestricted individual-level monotonicity class and the aggregate monotone \(\Gamma\)-Lipschitz mean class are incomparable; the former strengthens aggregation while the latter strengthens smoothness.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Choose \(a_1\in\mathcal A\setminus\{a_0\}\).  For the first witness, set
\[
Y_i(a_1,t)=\mathbf 1\{t>1/2\}
\]
for every unit, and set all other nonneutral outcomes to zero and all neutral outcomes to zero.  This array is bounded, every nonneutral trajectory is nondecreasing, and every neutral trajectory is constant, so it belongs to \(\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO}}\).  Its cell mean for action \(a_1\) is the same step function.  If \(\Gamma=0\), any two points straddling \(1/2\) violate the aggregate Lipschitz condition.  If \(\Gamma>0\), choose
\[
0<\varepsilon<\min\{1/2,1/\Gamma\}.
\]
Between \(s=1/2\) and \(t=1/2+\varepsilon\), the mean changes by one whereas \(\Gamma|t-s|<1\).  Thus this array is not in \(\mathcal M_N\).

For the reverse witness, choose distinct \(i_1,i_2\) with \(x_{i_1}=x_{i_2}=x_\star\), and define for action \(a_1\)
\[
Y_{i_1}(a_1,t)=1-t,
\qquad
Y_{i_2}(a_1,t)=t,
\qquad
Y_i(a_1,t)=\frac12
\quad\text{for every other }i\text{ in cell }x_\star.
\]
Set the action-\(a_1\) outcomes in other cells to \(1/2\), all remaining nonneutral outcomes to zero, and all neutral outcomes to zero.  The cell mean at \((x_\star,a_1)\) is
\[
\frac{(1-t)+t+(N_{x_\star}-2)/2}{N_{x_\star}}=\frac12,
\]
and every other cell-mean trajectory is constant.  Hence all cell means are monotone and \(\Gamma\)-Lipschitz for every \(\Gamma\geq0\), and neutral means are invariant, so the array belongs to \(\mathcal M_N\).  But \(t\mapsto Y_{i_1}(a_1,t)=1-t\) is strictly decreasing, so the array is not in \(\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO}}\).  The two explicit witnesses prove incomparability.
added_lemmas.justification: The two explicit arrays prevent a false claim that the aggregate mean assumptions are simply the published assumptions in different notation.
added_lemmas.gap: The class comparison is bookkeeping for the bridge to ChenOberst2025, not a new causal estimand or an additional design result.
added_lemmas.consumer: Readers can see exactly which heterogeneity and discontinuity patterns distinguish the two unrestricted classes.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every selected mean table \(y\) compatible with \(\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO}}\), the no-Lipschitz envelopes are bounded and nondecreasing for nonneutral actions, constant for the neutral action, agree with every matching anchor, and satisfy
\[
\ell^{\mathrm{CO}}_{xa}(t;y)\leq\mu_{xa}(t)\leq u^{\mathrm{CO}}_{xa}(t;y)
\]
for every compatible induced mean surface \(\mu\).  In particular, \(\ell^{\mathrm{CO}}_{xa}(t;y)\leq u^{\mathrm{CO}}_{xa}(t;y)\) for all \((x,a,t)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a compatible array and its induced mean surface \(\mu\).  Averaging the unit-level inequalities in \(\mathrm{def{:}chen\text{-}oberst\text{-}individual\text{-}class}\) shows that \(t\mapsto\mu_{xa}(t)\) is nondecreasing when \(a\neq a_0\), and that \(t\mapsto\mu_{x a_0}(t)\) is constant.  If \(a\neq a_0\), every matching anchor with \(m_c\leq t\) satisfies
\[
y_{cx}=\mu_{xa}(m_c)\leq\mu_{xa}(t),
\]
whereas every matching anchor with \(m_c\geq t\) satisfies
\[
\mu_{xa}(t)\leq\mu_{xa}(m_c)=y_{cx}.
\]
Together with \(0\leq\mu_{xa}(t)\leq1\), taking the maximum of all lower inequalities and the minimum of all upper inequalities yields
\[
\ell^{\mathrm{CO}}_{xa}(t;y)\leq\mu_{xa}(t)\leq u^{\mathrm{CO}}_{xa}(t;y).
\tag{1}
\]
As \(t\) increases, the anchor set in the lower maximum can only grow, while the anchor set in the upper minimum can only shrink.  Therefore both envelopes are nondecreasing.  At an anchor score \(t=m_d\), the defining lower maximum contains \(y_{dx}\), the defining upper minimum contains \(y_{dx}\), and (1) is centered at \(\mu_{xa}(m_d)=y_{dx}\); hence both envelopes equal \(y_{dx}\).

For \(a=a_0\), compatibility and unit-level neutral invariance imply that all matching anchor values equal one common number.  If there is an anchor, both neutral formulas therefore equal that number; if there is none, they are the constants zero and one.  Thus the neutral envelopes are constant, bounded, agree with all anchors, and satisfy (1).  Finally (1) directly implies the asserted order between the two envelopes.
added_lemmas.justification: This is the monotonicity-only interpolation fact needed to obtain the faithful no-Lipschitz corollary.
added_lemmas.gap: Unlike the \(\Gamma\)-Lipschitz envelopes, these endpoints use only order relative to the target score.
added_lemmas.consumer: The no-Lipschitz sharpness theorem uses the lemma to compute endpoints without importing smoothness.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(S\in\mathcal P_k\), every selected mean table \(y\) compatible with \(\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO}}\), and every \(\pi\in\mathcal F\), the identified set for \(V_\mu(\pi)\) over \(\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO}}\) conditional on \(y\) is exactly \(\mathcal I^{\mathrm{CO}}_S(\pi;y)\).  One homogeneous-within-cell array attains all lower endpoints and one such array attains all upper endpoints simultaneously over \(\mathcal F\).  Moreover,
\[
\overline W^{\mathrm{CO}}(S)
=\max_{\pi\in\mathcal F}R^{\mathrm{CO}}_\pi(S)
=\max_{\pi\in\mathcal F}\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}q_x
\min\bigl(\{1\}\cup\{d^{\mathrm{CO}}_{\pi xc}:c\in S\}\bigr),
\]
and the supremum is attained by two observationally indistinguishable homogeneous fixed arrays.  For every \((\pi,x)\), \(r^{\mathrm{CO}}_{\pi x}(S)=0\) exactly when a selected candidate uses the matching neutral action, or uses the matching nonneutral action at exactly the target score; \(r^{\mathrm{CO}}_{\pi x}(S)=1\) otherwise.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(S\), a compatible \(y\), and an induced mean surface \(\mu\) from \(\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO}}\).  The no-Lipschitz envelope-feasibility lemma gives, cell by cell,
\[
\ell^{\mathrm{CO}}_{x,\pi(x)}(m_\pi;y)
\leq\mu_{x,\pi(x)}(m_\pi)
\leq u^{\mathrm{CO}}_{x,\pi(x)}(m_\pi;y).
\]
Multiplication by \(q_x>0\), summation, and the definitions of \(L^{\mathrm{CO}}_S\), \(U^{\mathrm{CO}}_S\), and \(V_\mu\) yield
\[
L^{\mathrm{CO}}_S(\pi;y)
\leq V_\mu(\pi)
\leq U^{\mathrm{CO}}_S(\pi;y).
\tag{1}
\]
Define \(\mu^-_{xa}=\ell^{\mathrm{CO}}_{xa}\) and \(\mu^+_{xa}=u^{\mathrm{CO}}_{xa}\), and set \(Y_i^\pm(a,t)=\mu^\pm_{x_i a}(t)\).  The envelope-feasibility lemma shows that these homogeneous arrays are bounded, unitwise nondecreasing for nonneutral actions, unitwise constant for the neutral action, and compatible with every anchor.  Hence \(Y^\pm\in\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO}}\), both generate \(y\), and, simultaneously for every \(\pi\in\mathcal F\),
\[
V_{\mu^-}(\pi)=L^{\mathrm{CO}}_S(\pi;y),
\qquad
V_{\mu^+}(\pi)=U^{\mathrm{CO}}_S(\pi;y).
\tag{2}
\]
For \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), the convex combination \((1-\lambda)Y^-+\lambda Y^+\) remains in \(\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO}}\), preserves the anchors, and has value
\[
(1-\lambda)L^{\mathrm{CO}}_S(\pi;y)
+\lambda U^{\mathrm{CO}}_S(\pi;y).
\]
Thus every point of the interval in (1) is attained, proving conditional sharpness and the common-schedule assertion.

It remains to compute the prospective diameter.  From the cost definition,
\[
r^{\mathrm{CO}}_{\pi x}(S)=0
\]
exactly if \(S\) contains a candidate \(c\) with either \(c(x)=\pi(x)=a_0\), or \(c(x)=\pi(x)\neq a_0\) and \(m_c=m_\pi\); otherwise \(r^{\mathrm{CO}}_{\pi x}(S)=1\).  In the first case the matching observation is at the target response: neutral invariance identifies every score for the neutral action, and exact score matching directly identifies a nonneutral response.  Therefore the two envelopes agree at the target.  In the second case their gap is at most one by boundedness.  In both cases,
\[
u^{\mathrm{CO}}_{x,\pi(x)}(m_\pi;y)
-\ell^{\mathrm{CO}}_{x,\pi(x)}(m_\pi;y)
\leq r^{\mathrm{CO}}_{\pi x}(S).
\tag{3}
\]
Summing (3), maximizing over \(\pi\), and taking the supremum over \(\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO}}\) proves
\[
\overline W^{\mathrm{CO}}(S)
\leq\max_{\pi\in\mathcal F}R^{\mathrm{CO}}_\pi(S).
\tag{4}
\]

Choose a maximizer \(\pi^\star\), which exists because \(\mathcal F\) is finite and nonempty.  Fix a cell, put \(a=\pi^\star(x)\), \(t=m_{\pi^\star}\), and \(w=r^{\mathrm{CO}}_{\pi^\star x}(S)\in\{0,1\}\).  If \(w=0\), use the identical zero function in the two schedules.  If \(w=1\) and \(a\neq a_0\), use
\[
g_x^-(s)=\mathbf 1\{s>t\},
\qquad
g_x^+(s)=\mathbf 1\{s\geq t\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Both functions are bounded and nondecreasing.  Because \(w=1\), no selected matching-action anchor has score exactly \(t\).  At every matching selected score below \(t\), both functions in (5) are zero, and at every such score above \(t\), both are one.  Thus they agree at every matching anchor but satisfy \(g_x^-(t)=0\) and \(g_x^+(t)=1\).  If \(w=1\) and \(a=a_0\), there is no selected matching neutral anchor, so use the two constants zero and one.

Use this pair for action \(\pi^\star(x)\) in each cell and the identical zero function for all other actions, and homogenize within each cell.  The resulting two arrays lie in \(\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO}}\), agree at every selected arm-cell observation, and have value separation
\[
V_{\mu^+}(\pi^\star)-V_{\mu^-}(\pi^\star)
=\sum_xq_xr^{\mathrm{CO}}_{\pi^\star x}(S)
=R^{\mathrm{CO}}_{\pi^\star}(S).
\tag{6}
\]
Conditional sharpness puts the two values in the same identified interval for their common table.  Hence (6) gives the reverse of (4), proves attainment, and establishes the displayed width identity.  The stated zero-cost characterization follows directly from the two zero cases in the definition of \(d^{\mathrm{CO}}_{\pi xc}\).
added_lemmas.justification: This theorem gives the actual monotonicity-only sharp intervals and prospective width for the published individual-level class, including common endpoint schedules.
added_lemmas.gap: ChenOberst2025 proves tight reusable-validation bounds without a Lipschitz assumption; this corollary exposes the resulting exact finite-panel prospective cost and distinguishes it from the finite-\(\Gamma\) nearest-score geometry.
added_lemmas.consumer: A designer unwilling to impose score smoothness can compute the exact robust panel loss using only exact target-score or neutral-action matches.

proposed.name: Fixed-population individual-level Chen--Oberst class
proposed.construction:
Define the fixed-population individual-level Chen--Oberst class by
\[
\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO}}
=\left\{Y\in[0,1]^{\mathcal I\times\mathcal A\times[0,1]}:
\begin{array}{l}
Y_i(a,s)\leq Y_i(a,t)\text{ for every }i\in\mathcal I,
a\in\mathcal A\setminus\{a_0\},0\leq s\leq t\leq1,\\
Y_i(a_0,s)=Y_i(a_0,t)\text{ for every }i\in\mathcal I,
s,t\in[0,1]
\end{array}\right\}.
\]
The range restriction in the ambient product is the bounded-outcome condition.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Define the faithful bounded unit-level monotonicity and neutral-equality class requested by the directive.

proposed.name: Individual-level Chen--Oberst Lipschitz subclass
proposed.construction:
Define its individual-level Lipschitz refinement by
\[
\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO},\Gamma}
=\left\{Y\in\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO}}:
|Y_i(a,t)-Y_i(a,s)|\leq\Gamma|t-s|
\text{ for every }i\in\mathcal I,
a\in\mathcal A\setminus\{a_0\},s,t\in[0,1]\right\}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: Define the unit-level Lipschitz subclass on which the finite-\(\Gamma\) headline remains exact.

proposed.name: Chen--Oberst monotonicity-only envelopes
proposed.construction:
For \(S\in\mathcal P_k\), a compatible selected mean table \(y\), and \(t\in[0,1]\), define, when \(a\neq a_0\),
\[
\ell^{\mathrm{CO}}_{xa}(t;y)
=\max\bigl(\{0\}\cup\{y_{cx}:c\in T_{xa}(S),\ m_c\leq t\}\bigr),
\qquad
u^{\mathrm{CO}}_{xa}(t;y)
=\min\bigl(\{1\}\cup\{y_{cx}:c\in T_{xa}(S),\ m_c\geq t\}\bigr).
\]
For \(a=a_0\), define
\[
\ell^{\mathrm{CO}}_{x a_0}(t;y)
=\max\bigl(\{0\}\cup\{y_{cx}:c\in T_{x a_0}(S)\}\bigr),
\qquad
u^{\mathrm{CO}}_{x a_0}(t;y)
=\min\bigl(\{1\}\cup\{y_{cx}:c\in T_{x a_0}(S)\}\bigr).
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: Expose the computable sharp envelopes for the actual no-Lipschitz class.

proposed.name: Chen--Oberst reusable policy interval
proposed.construction:
For \(\pi\in\mathcal F\), define
\[
L^{\mathrm{CO}}_S(\pi;y)
=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}q_x\ell^{\mathrm{CO}}_{x,\pi(x)}(m_\pi;y),
\qquad
U^{\mathrm{CO}}_S(\pi;y)
=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}q_xu^{\mathrm{CO}}_{x,\pi(x)}(m_\pi;y),
\]
and \(\mathcal I^{\mathrm{CO}}_S(\pi;y)=[L^{\mathrm{CO}}_S(\pi;y),U^{\mathrm{CO}}_S(\pi;y)]\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Define the causal policy-value interval induced by the monotonicity-only envelopes.

proposed.name: Chen--Oberst exact-match prospective loss
proposed.construction:
For \(\pi\in\mathcal F\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(c\in\mathcal C\), define
\[
d^{\mathrm{CO}}_{\pi xc}
=\begin{cases}
0,&c(x)=\pi(x)=a_0,\\
0,&c(x)=\pi(x)\neq a_0\text{ and }m_c=m_\pi,\\
1,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
and set
\[
r^{\mathrm{CO}}_{\pi x}(S)
=\min\bigl(\{1\}\cup\{d^{\mathrm{CO}}_{\pi xc}:c\in S\}\bigr),
\qquad
R^{\mathrm{CO}}_\pi(S)
=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}q_xr^{\mathrm{CO}}_{\pi x}(S).
\]
The no-Lipschitz prospective loss is
\[
\overline W^{\mathrm{CO}}(S)
=\sup_{Y\in\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO}}}
\max_{\pi\in\mathcal F}
\left\{U^{\mathrm{CO}}_S(\pi;y(Y))-L^{\mathrm{CO}}_S(\pi;y(Y))\right\}.
\]

proposed.statement: For every \(S\in\mathcal P_k\), every compatible \(y\), and every \(\pi\in\mathcal F\), the identified set for \(V_{\mu}(\pi)\) over \(\mathcal M_N\) conditional on \(y\) is exactly \([L_S(\pi;y),U_S(\pi;y)]\). One response schedule \(\mu^{-}\) attains all lower endpoints and one response schedule \(\mu^{+}\) attains all upper endpoints simultaneously over \(\mathcal F\).

The worst-case regret is approximately equal---and sometimes exactly equal---to the objective function of a k-median problem.

prose_updates.tldr: One randomized panel of deterministic machine-learning policies must support sharp causal validation of a prespecified update library. The finite-\(\Gamma\) nearest-matching-score width is exact both for the aggregate cell-mean class and for a source-faithful individual-level Chen--Oberst subclass, because homogenization makes their induced mean surfaces coincide. Under the actual bounded no-Lipschitz Chen--Oberst class, the exact prospective cell cost is zero only for a selected matching neutral arm or a selected matching nonneutral arm at exactly the target score, and is one otherwise; homogeneous common endpoint schedules prove sharpness. The rational mixed-integer panel optimization and simultaneous assignment-only coverage remain supporting design and inference results.

project_justification.gap: ChenOberst2025 supplies tight monotonicity-only reusable-validation bounds under unit-level performance monotonicity and neutral-action equality, but not the finite-\(\Gamma\) prospective nearest-score panel identity. AnthonyGoyalGuptaNagarajan2010 supplies the robust scenario nearest-facility skeleton, MontielOleaPrallonQiuStoyeSun2025 supplies the closest causal \(k\)-median analogy, and HochbaumPathria1998 supplies the zero-sensitivity maximum-coverage boundary.
project_justification.niche: The field niche is the causal derivation of the exact design loss: a faithful bridge shows that the finite-\(\Gamma\) common-schedule and width results remain exact on an individual-level Chen--Oberst subclass, while a separate theorem recovers the genuine no-Lipschitz class with its exact binary matching geometry.
project_justification.fill: The project proves common sharp endpoint schedules and attained prospective causal-width identities for both regimes, a rational budget-optimal panel formulation, and simultaneous randomization-only outer coverage. The mixed-integer program, exhaustive branch certificate, maximum-coverage reduction, and explicit rational instance are implementation and falsification infrastructure rather than the field novelty.

sampling_model.units: The covariates \(x_i\) and full bounded potential-outcome schedules \(Y_i(a,t)\) are fixed; only assignment \(Z\) is random. The source-faithful finite-\(\Gamma\) formulation ranges over \(\mathcal M_N^{\mathrm{CO},\Gamma}\); the aggregate class \(\mathcal M_N\) is a mean-level enlargement with exactly the same induced cell-mean surfaces, selected means, and policy values.

prose_updates.related_work: Chen and Oberst (2025, Introduction, Section 4, Remark 3.1, and Appendix D.1) study reusable validation under bounded unit-level performance monotonicity and unit-level neutral-action equality, without a Lipschitz restriction, and prove tight bounds. The present conditional-mean monotonicity and neutral invariance are relaxations in aggregation, whereas finite \(\Gamma\)-Lipschitz smoothness is a refinement; the two unrestricted classes are incomparable. A homogenization bridge proves that the individual-level \(\Gamma\)-Lipschitz subclass and the aggregate class generate the same mean surfaces, and a separate no-Lipschitz theorem recovers the exact Chen--Oberst regime with binary exact-score or neutral matching costs. Anthony, Goyal, Gupta, and Nagarajan (2010, Section 2 and Theorem 2.2) supply the robust min-max \(k\)-median skeleton; the metric lift is informed by that result and does not claim its approximation theory. Montiel Olea, Prallon, Qiu, Stoye, and Sun (2025, Theorem 1 and Appendix A.2) connect causal site selection to \(k\)-median for a different estimand. Hochbaum and Pathria (1998) supply the maximum-\(k\)-coverage benchmark. Cheung, Gleixner, and Steffy (2017) and Szeider (2026) motivate exact rational proof logs. Caughey, Dafoe, Li, and Miratrix (2023) study finite-sample randomization-only simultaneous inference for a different causal family, while Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey (2021) study adaptive policy evaluation. Hoeffding (1963) supplies the sampling-without-replacement concentration comparison.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The common endpoint schedules establish simultaneous marginal lower and upper corners, not rectangularity of the full joint value set. The aggregate mean class and the no-Lipschitz individual-level class are not interchangeable: neither contains the other on nondegenerate populations. Exact score-distance gains require the finite-\(\Gamma\) subclass; monotonicity alone yields only binary exact-score or neutral-action protection. The facility-location lift does not transfer a published approximation ratio to every implementation convention. The exhaustive certificate can be exponential, and the outer confidence intervals are conservative rather than shortest. Scores, libraries, \(\Gamma\), and the budget are fixed before assignment.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The field obligations are the common causal endpoint schedules, the exact prospective widths derived from observationally indistinguishable fixed arrays, the faithful bridge to the individual-level Chen--Oberst class, and simultaneous assignment-only coverage. The finite-\(\Gamma\) identity is exact on the individual-level Lipschitz subclass and on the larger aggregate mean class because their induced mean surfaces coincide; it is not attributed to the published no-Lipschitz assumptions. For that actual no-Lipschitz class, the proved prospective cost is binary. The project does not claim a rectangular joint value set, optimize allocation, estimate future scores, or supply a polynomial exact algorithm on unrestricted instances.
